executiveSummary: GM1966's 2025 identity, centre, population, 63 neighbourhoods, 45 BAG places, 118 settlement labels, ten railway stations and eleven NWB border links are internally coherent, apart from one explicitly retained Warffum label-point/generalized-boundary caveat. The complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The generic coastal preset produces 2.476450 m direct depth, 22,589 maximum resident-equivalent exposure and 1,678,953.659 deprived person-hours without selecting a Wadden Sea level, primary-defence state, breach/overtopping location, Lauwersmeer state, arrival, duration or dewatering curve. Official evidence instead distinguishes the Wadden Sea primary coast, Lauwersmeerdijk works, regional Lauwersmeer storage, R.J. Clevering sluices, boezem discharge and pumping. A source placed at the reviewed 21 August 2026 KNMI Zandeweer earthquake origin lies in Buitengebied Kantens but that neighbourhood ranks only eighteenth, while a source placed inside the official Marnewaard combustible polygon leaves Lauwersmeer twenty-second. Eight active hazards reuse the same leading neighbourhood order. Eemshaven has an official zero resident population but 127 non-residential buildings and 50 businesses; it ranks thirty-fifth and contributes zero affected residents even during the coastal, earthquake and compound exercises, despite public-authority evidence of its nationally important energy, LNG, cable, port, passenger and hazardous-site functions. The eleven-edge road-only logical network likewise does not represent ten rail stations, Eemshaven/Lauwersoog maritime links or their transfer dependencies. Public observation, forecast, register and planning layers can constrain an exercise, but none establishes live defence, pump, port, facility, utility, transport, occupancy or recovery state. Unknown and NoData must never be presented as zero or safe, and exact local consequences remain synthetic until a source-valid scenario and action ledger are approved.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1966 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM1966 as Het Hogeland in Groningen and reports 48,178 residents, density 101/km², 26.2% aged 65 or older and 7,931 one-person households; the generated centre [6.49705631506127, 53.37704257776893] lies inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Sixty-three published neighbourhood rows in fourteen districts sum to 48,175 residents, three below the municipality total (-0.006%); households sum to 21,975 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 12,610. Allocation reconciles to 48,178 without rewriting source observations.

BAG supplies 45 active woonplaatsen and BRT supplies 118 settlement labels—53 woonkernen, 34 buurtschappen, 27 gehuchten and four deelkernen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0; labels are not occupancy, catchment, defence or service footprints.

The BAG Warffum label point [6.546754309363411, 53.45990841858407] falls outside the independently versioned CBS generalized polygon. This bounded geometry/edition result is preserved for review, not silently snapped or used to exclude Warffum. Home value and several benefit/access fields cover 62/63 neighbourhoods, cars per household 59/63, and district heat and charging 0/63; missing, suppressed and non-applicable source values remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Adopted Regional Crisis-management Policy Plan 2024–2028 and current Groningen threat catalogue
evidenceSources.edition: Regionaal Beleidsplan Crisisbeheersing 2024–2028, adopted 12 July 2024; current public risk pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The adopted plan's 2024 risk profile covers transport and chemical accidents, large fires, sea/regional flooding, drought/heat, nature fire, extreme weather, earthquakes, energy, drinking-water, ICT/telecom and cyber disruption. It expressly treats impact as scenario- and local-condition-dependent and no longer assigns false quantitative probabilities or priorities.

Its regional trends include climate change, energy transition, subsurface developments, digitalization/cyber, demography and self-reliance. Effects include primary-needs shortage, economic disruption, environmental harm and disruption of daily life; this is risk-selection and governance evidence, not an incident or municipality forecast.

The current authority list identifies Eems Energy Terminal and VOPAK Eemshaven as facilities with ramp-response plans and says such plans are updated every eighteen months. Publication of a facility name and update policy does not reveal current inventories, contours, staffing, alarms, response resources or plan validity for a chosen exercise.

The PDF/pages are public documentary evidence with regional/local relevance, explicit policy dates, no machine event cadence and no standard redistribution licence identified. Exact local likelihood, casualties, plume, outage, dispatch and restoration remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Noorderzijlvest / Stuurgroep Lauwersmeer / Gemeente Het Hogeland
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027 and Toekomstagenda Lauwersmeer 2024 water-system pathways
evidenceSources.edition: Noorderzijlvest Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027; Lauwersmeer agenda map dated 18 January 2024; project status pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The water programme distinguishes primary Wadden Sea defences, regional defences, outer-dike port, Lauwersmeer storage, main discharge areas and pumping. It calls for defence assessment, flood-storage and water-system capacity work rather than one municipality-wide depth curve.

The joint Lauwersmeer agenda states that Noorderzijlvest and Wetterskip Fryslân manage different defences, that Lauwersmeer is a regional storage basin, and that excess Groningen/Fryslân water drains via R.J. Clevering sluices to the Wadden Sea. High sea levels reduce free-discharge windows; prolonged rain, boezem levels, Waterwolf and Hunsingo pumping are coupled pathways.

Official 2026 project reporting says electrically driven Hunsingo pumping at Zoutkamp with 1,600 m³/min capacity and regional-defence works were completed. The Lauwersmeerdijk–Vierhuizergat primary-defence project covers approximately nine kilometres and remains a separately governed project. Design/project capacity is not event availability or delivered flow.

These are public programme/project documents with dated regional/local coverage, no standard machine cadence and no standard redistribution licence found. They support topology and action review but not live gates, pumps, defences, boezem level, salinity, capacity, failure or recovery.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — LIWO 2025.1.6 professional flood layers and Waterinfo Wadden Sea observation/forecast context
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6 announced 30 October 2025; Waterinfo snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: LIWO provides professional flood-preparedness layers and explicitly requires specialist water-manager interpretation. A governed adapter must select source, scenario, defence/breach state, depth/datum, arrival, duration, recession, resolution, valid time, uncertainty, coverage, NoData and licence; LIWO availability is not permission to invent a local event.

The deployed CC0 Waterinfo context contains one fresh point observation at Lauwersoog Wadden Sea: -66 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026, retrieved 33 minutes later. It also contains Wadden Sea forecast points at requested T+1/6/12/24/48, while the national public endpoint returned no T+72 water-level forecasts.

Waterinfo forecasts are official guidance points, not defence states, breach models or municipal inundation depths. T+72 absence and any absent station/horizon are NoData, never zero water or safety. Values from 2–3 September cannot silently drive a calendar-unbound synthetic scenario.

Waterinfo states CC0 unless component-specific terms differ, generally ten-minute LMW observations, frontend forecast endpoints without a stable external service contract, point coverage rather than a surface, and public service not mission-critical. LIWO licence and download constraints must be resolved per selected layer/release.

evidenceSources.publisher: Koninklijk Nederlands Meteorologisch Instituut / Nationaal Coördinator Groningen
evidenceSources.title: E05 — KNMI FDSN seismic origins and building-strengthening context
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI rolling 365-day catalogue retrieved 2 September 2026; NCG public strengthening status inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The CC BY 4.0 KNMI event catalogue contains four reviewed induced/triggered origins inside GM1966 during the covered year: Usquert M0.93, two Uithuizen events M1.10/M1.80 and Zandeweer M2.7566 at [6.667, 53.378], depth 3 km, origin 21 August 2026 03:50:39Z. Origins can be revised and are not ground-motion, felt-intensity, damage or probability surfaces.

Polygon containment places the Zandeweer origin in CBS neighbourhood Buitengebied Kantens. A controlled simulator source at that coordinate produces 0.127536 g and 12,977 affected resident-equivalents at T+6 but ranks the source-containing neighbourhood eighteenth of 63, behind the same generic leading areas used by unrelated hazards.

NCG confirms that Het Hogeland schools and buildings form part of the strengthening programme; examples in Kantens and Uithuizen show completed, ongoing and planned works. Programme inclusion or an individual strengthened building cannot be generalized into a municipal fragility, completion or occupancy value.

The FDSN catalogue updates as events are published, covers a bounded 365-day/bounding-box query and applies the RDSA default CC BY 4.0 licence. No catalogued event means no origin in that scope, not zero seismic hazard. NCG documentary pages have project-specific dates and no standard machine cadence/licence identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Groningen Seaports / Gemeente Het Hogeland / Veiligheidsregio Groningen
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Eemshaven national energy, deep-water, industrial and maritime dependency context
evidenceSources.edition: Groningen Seaports 2025 facts; municipal Port Defender exercise 13 April 2026; risk-company page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The public port authority describes Eemshaven as an 8,000 MW energy hub, around one-third of national generation, with three power stations, 112 onshore turbines, Norway/Denmark submarine connections, an LNG terminal, four basins, 5,293 m quay, 14 m depth and 10,748,967 tonnes 2025 transshipment. These are static/annual facts, not incident capacity or availability.

The municipality's April 2026 Port Defender exercise involved a Borkum passenger ferry, maritime intervention, victim care and passenger reception and identifies Eemshaven energy plants, LNG, submarine cables and port/NATO functions as nationally material dependencies. Exercise narrative is not a current threat, passenger count or response commitment.

CBS nevertheless publishes Eemshaven neighbourhood population zero alongside one home, 127 non-residential buildings, 50 businesses and ten cars. Resident population cannot represent workers, mariners, passengers, contractors or national downstream customers; their incident-time counts remain Unknown.

Groningen Seaports and municipal/VRG pages are public documentary/annual context with site-level relevance, source dates or reporting year, no stable machine status feed and no standard redistribution licence identified. Do not convert installed power, tonnes, quays or named facilities into emergency output, topology, live stock, occupancy or restoration.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — NWB roads, rail stations, scheduled transit and observed road-situation context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB logical graph has eleven border links over N33, N46, N361, N363, N388, N983, N993, N996 and N998 toward Eemsdelta, Groningen, Noardeast-Fryslân and Westerkwartier. Each nominal 150 is a scenario unit, and same-corridor series links must not be summed as physical capacity.

The CC0 ProRail register places ten stations inside the boundary—Sauwerd, Baflo, Eemshaven, Warffum, Roodeschool, Bedum, Usquert, Winsum, Uithuizermeeden and Uithuizen—and GTFS contains 158 stop areas including Lauwersoog ferry-harbour and Eemshaven labels. Static geometry and best-effort schedules do not prove operations, passengers, accessibility, capacity or recovery.

All eleven service-flow edges are road-derived: rail, ferry and deep-water port transfers have no explicit logical dependency or failure state. The Borkum and Lauwersoog passenger/vehicle connections, port basins and rail can be represented only as transparent typed scenario proxies until operator-approved operational feeds exist.

The timestamped CC0 NDW snapshot assigns zero current situations to GM1966. This is no matching covered record at retrieval time, never proof that roads, crossings, rail, ferries, ports or transit are open. Register, schedule and observation evidence classes remain separate.

evidenceSources.publisher: BIJ12/IPO Risicokaart; Het Waterschapshuis; Netbeheer Nederland; RDI; DUO; RIVM; KNMI; Rijkswaterstaat
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public nature-fire, water-asset, grid-planning, communications, education, care and weather context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; Risicokaart catalogue updated 16 October 2024
supports: The CC BY 4.0 Risicokaart WFS returns three GM1966-supplied combustible areas in the municipal bounding extent: Ballastplaat and Vlinderbalgbos (deciduous woodland) and Marnewaard (mixed woodland), valid from 13 January 2006. A point [6.23, 53.40] intersects Marnewaard and CBS neighbourhood Lauwersmeer, but a controlled T+24 fire ranks that neighbourhood twenty-second while assigning municipality smoke 0.361861, flame 0.084838 and 2,431 affected resident-equivalents.

The partial HWH IMWA/DAMO CC BY-SA 4.0 aggregation contains zero matched water assets in GM1966 despite authoritative documentary evidence of major sluice/pump/defence assets. This demonstrates contributor/geometry coverage limits: zero matching points is not no assets, capacity or safe drainage.

One Winsum-Ranum NBNL planning sample reports 176.8 MW existing withdrawal, 52.6 MW required, 12.2 MW queued and 40 requests; injection 171.8/77.2/5.4 MW and 23 requests, TenneT classes 3/3 and five projects from 2027. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning data with an unstated exact licence is not Eemshaven coverage, current load, reserve, outage or topology.

The municipality contains 201 RDI antenna installations—67 mobile, 69 fixed-link, eight other-mobile, 56 amateur and one broadcast—and 39 daily CC-BY DUO education locations. RDI states no standard licence/cadence. Zero RIVM acute-care, air-quality, KNMI weather-station and NDW point matches mean no covered record, not no care, exposure, weather or disruption; the Groningen province warning snapshot was level zero at retrieval, not an exercise all-clear. Every context family has affectsSimulation=false.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, municipality centre and resident totals reconcile.
findings.evidence: GM1966, Het Hogeland, Groningen and Veiligheidsregio Groningen agree; the centre is contained. CBS reports 48,178 residents and 63 neighbourhoods sum to 48,175 (-0.006%).
findings.action: Retain source editions, licence, null semantics and reconciliation metadata without rewriting the three-person publication difference.

findings.summary: Warffum's BAG label point falls outside the independently versioned generalized CBS boundary.
findings.evidence: The audit context reproduces one mismatch at [6.546754309363411, 53.45990841858407]; other official municipal, neighbourhood and place identities remain coherent.
findings.action: Retain Warffum and expose the edition/generalization caveat. Compare full-resolution BAG woonplaats and CBS gemeente polygons before changing geometry; never snap a point or infer exclusion from generalized containment alone.

findings.summary: The generic coastal-distance function emits an unsupported exact 2.476450 m direct depth.
findings.evidence: At T+6/T+24 the canonical coastal preset reaches severity 0.754843 and direct depth 2.476450 m, affecting up to 22,589 resident-equivalents, without selecting Wadden Sea boundary level, defence, breach/overtopping, compartment, Lauwersmeer/boezem state, arrival, duration or recession. Official evidence distinguishes these mechanisms.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing GM1966 direct depth/exposure until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/Noorderzijlvest/RWS event intersects the boundary. Retain coast proximity only as an unsupported diagnostic and retain Wadden Sea, Ems-Dollard, Lauwersmeer, boezem, polder, seepage, pluvial and drainage mechanisms as separate Unknown states.

findings.summary: Lauwersmeer storage, free discharge, boezem and pumping dependencies are absent from the causal water model.
findings.evidence: The authority describes R.J. Clevering discharge windows, Lauwersmeer storage, two water-board systems and Waterwolf/Hunsingo pumping. The partial HWH point aggregation nevertheless has zero GM1966 matches, proving a coverage gap rather than no assets.
findings.action: Add a typed public-evidence water graph with distinct sea boundary, primary/regional defence, basin, boezem, sluice and pump states. Bind project/design capacity only when event validity and operator state are supplied; otherwise use Unknown and a transparent synthetic fallback.

findings.summary: An explicit local earthquake source does not control neighbourhood shaking allocation.
findings.evidence: KNMI's reviewed M2.7566 Zandeweer origin at [6.667,53.378] lies in Buitengebied Kantens. A controlled source at that point produces 0.127536 g and 12,977 affected residents at T+6, but the source neighbourhood ranks eighteenth behind the generic cross-hazard order.
findings.action: Make source coordinates, event depth/magnitude, a cited ground-motion model, soil/building inputs and uncertainty govern local shaking. Add a regression that the source-containing region is spatially responsive; never equate the observed M2.7566 origin with the stronger synthetic scenario.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse one neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber, wildfire and compound active checkpoints all rank Buitengebied Uithuizermeeden, Zuidwolde, Sauwerd, Pieterburen and Den Andel first in the same order; Eemshaven is thirty-fifth.
findings.action: Replace the common seed with hazard-specific physical surfaces and exposed-object intersections. Preserve deterministic tie-breaking only after evidence-derived values and keep unsupported cells Unknown rather than pseudo-precise.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure erases Eemshaven workers, passengers, industrial activity and national dependencies.
findings.evidence: CBS publishes zero residents but 127 non-residential buildings and 50 businesses in Eemshaven. The region consequently contributes zero affected residents in coastal, earthquake and compound results, while port/VRG evidence identifies nationally material energy, LNG, cable, maritime and ramp-plan functions.
findings.action: Keep official resident zero, but add separate timestamped worker/visitor/passenger/activity and critical-service exposure dimensions when an authoritative source is available. Until then display those populations and external consequences as Unknown; never manufacture persons from buildings, businesses, installed MW or annual tonnes.

findings.summary: Road-only logical flows omit ten stations, ferry links, deep-water port transfers and modal coupling.
findings.evidence: The graph exposes eleven NWB road edges only. ProRail lists ten stations, GTFS has 158 stop areas including port/ferry labels, and municipal/GSP evidence confirms passenger and maritime operations, but no rail/ferry/port edge or transfer state affects mobility or supply.
findings.action: Add typed non-additive rail, ferry, port and transfer proxies with source, schedule/validity, passenger/freight scope, closure, alternative access and Unknown status. Do not claim measured throughput without operator evidence.

findings.summary: Official combustible polygons and an explicit local source do not govern fire allocation.
findings.evidence: Risicokaart returns Ballastplaat, Marnewaard and Vlinderbalgbos. A controlled source inside Marnewaard/Lauwersmeer produces T+24 flame 0.084838, smoke 0.361861 and 2,431 affected residents, but Lauwersmeer ranks twenty-second.
findings.action: Require selected ignition/perimeter, eligible vegetation, fuel/moisture, event-valid wind, access, extinguishing-water and suppression state. Use the CC BY 4.0 polygon only as eligibility/context, never as proof of ignition, current fuel or spread.

findings.summary: Zero matches, official zero residents and missing forecast horizons require distinct semantics.
findings.evidence: GM1966 has zero HWH assets, RIVM acute-care/air, local KNMI weather-station and NDW matches; Waterinfo has no national T+72 water-level forecast; Eemshaven has an official zero resident count. Each describes a different scope and none establishes no asset, care, weather, disruption, water or non-resident exposure.
findings.action: Render observed zero, no matching record, NoData, Unknown, outside coverage and not-applicable separately with source, valid time, coverage and affectsSimulation. Add contract tests that no absent record becomes zero, normal, safe or operational.

findings.summary: Rural ageing, care access and transient populations are not represented by the local facility context.

RIVM has zero covered acute-care respondent points inside GM1966, while rail/road/ferry and weather/water disruption can affect external access. findings.summary: First-72-hour restoration trajectories lack local operator and action evidence.
findings.evidence: Coastal burden reaches 1,678,953.659 person-hours by T+72, with 3,078 residents still affected after forcing falls to zero. Compound forcing remains nonzero with 21,880 affected and telecom availability 0.344544. No selected source supplies dewatering, port restart, utility restoration, multimodal reopening, care relocation or resource milestones.
findings.action: Add a causal action ledger for alerting, defence inspection/closure, sluice/pump decisions, evacuation/shelter/care, port and multimodal closure/reopening, utility isolation/restoration and public communication. Each action needs owner, trigger, request, decision, resource, dependency, execution, verification, valid time and rollback; otherwise label the curve synthetic.

residualLimitations: LIWO and water-manager scenario selection, defence/breach state, hydraulic connectivity, depth, arrival, duration, recession, dewatering and uncertainty have not been approved for GM1966.
Live Wadden Sea, Lauwersmeer, boezem, polder, salinity, groundwater, sewer, sluice, pump and defence states are unavailable to this audit.
The public HWH aggregation is contributor-dependent and has zero GM1966 matches; this is not an asset inventory or proof of absence.
KNMI origins do not supply a local ground-motion field, building fragility, damage, casualties or future-event probability.
NCG project pages do not provide an address-complete, event-valid strengthening/occupancy state suitable for open operational simulation.
Risicokaart combustible polygons are planning eligibility from 2006-era feature validity, not current vegetation, fuel, moisture, ignition or fire perimeter.
Eemshaven worker, contractor, ship, ferry passenger and visitor populations are not available as timestamped authoritative open data.
Installed energy capacity, annual cargo and named critical facilities do not expose live production, inventory, switching, reserve, vulnerability or restoration.
Electricity, drinking-water, gas and telecom physical topology, control, backup and restoration are unavailable or security-sensitive; no sensitive topology was inferred.
The one Winsum-Ranum capacity-map sample is not complete GM1966 or Eemshaven coverage and has no exact standard licence identifier.
ProRail, NWB and GTFS are static/register/schedule evidence; live train, bus, ferry, port and road availability and emergency throughput remain Unknown.
Zero NDW, RIVM acute-care/air and local KNMI weather-point matches are bounded no-match results, not absence or safety.
Waterinfo is point context from 2–3 September 2026 and cannot establish a municipal flood surface or silently drive a calendar-unbound exercise.
The Warffum BAG label-point mismatch requires full-resolution, edition-aligned polygon review and must not be auto-corrected from generalized geometry.
CBS residents and age/household context exclude temporary populations and do not support individual vulnerability labels or incident-time presence.
The public 2024–2028 risk profile is qualitative governance evidence and deliberately does not provide municipality probabilities or exact impacts.
No reviewed source validates the simulator's exact affected-resident, availability, person-hour or T+72 recovery values.
